title: Optimized fCUT&Tag-Seq Method for Profiling Histone Modifications in Fungi
author: Wang, Haiting

Mycelia were cross‐linked with a 1% formaldehyde solution (0.4 M sucrose, 10 mM Tris‐HCl [pH 8.0], 1 mM EDTA, 1 mM PMSF, 1% formaldehyde) at room temperature for 15 min, with the flask inverted every 2–3 min. To stop cross‐linking, glycine was added to a final concentration of 0.2 M, followed by incubation for 5 min. Fixed cells were then washed with 1× PBS, cryo‐milled in liquid nitrogen, and lysed in lysis buffer (50 mM HEPES [pH 7.5], 137 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 0.1% SDS, 1% Triton X‐100, 0.1% sodium deoxycholate, 1 mM PMSF, 1 μg/ml leupeptin, 1 μg/ml pepstatin A). Chromatin was sonicated to an average DNA fragment size of ~500–1000 bp. After sonication, samples were centrifuged at 10,000g and 4°C for 15 min to collect the supernatant. For immunoprecipitation, 2 μl of the anti‐H3K9ac antibody (Cat. No. 39161; Active Motif) was incubated with aliquots of clarified cell lysates (containing 2 mg of protein each) at 4°C overnight with rotation. After overnight incubation, 50 μl of SS DNA/Protein G Sepharose (pretreated three times with lysis buffer) was added, followed by further incubation at 4°C for 2 h. Sepharose beads were collected and washed once with 1 ml of each of the following buffers: high‐salt wash buffer (lysis buffer supplemented with 0.5 M NaCl), 1× LNDET (0.25 M LiCl, 1% NP40, 1% deoxycholate, 1 mM EDTA, 10 mM Tris [pH 8]), and 50 mM Tris‐HCl [pH 8], and 1 mM EDTA. Immune complexes were eluted from the beads using freshly prepared elution buffer (1% SDS, 0.1 M NaHCO₃) via two rounds of elution at room temperature (250 μl per elution).

steps.title: Prepare fungal protoplasts
steps.instruction: Digest mycelium or spores in species‑specific enzyme solution: for V. dahliae, N. crassa and S. scitamineum use 0.25 g VinoTaste®Pro enzyme in 12.5 ml 0.7 M NaCl; for F. graminearum use 0.1 g driselase, 0.2 g cellulase and 0.2 g lysozyme diluted to 20 ml with 0.7 M NaCl. Incubate 10 ml of this solution with the fungal material at 33 °C, 60 rpm (30 min for S. scitamineum spores, 3 h for mycelia) or at 30 °C, 85 rpm for F. graminearum. Filter the digestion through Miracloth (475855‑1 R; Merck), centrifuge 10 min at 3800 rpm (V. dahliae, N. crassa), 2200 rpm (S. scitamineum) or 5000 rpm (F. graminearum) at 25 °C, resuspend the pellet in 10 ml 0.7 M NaCl and count protoplasts with a hemocytometer.

steps.title: Extract nuclei from protoplasts
steps.instruction: Take 1 × 10⁶ protoplasts per 1.5 ml tube, centrifuge 5 min at 3000 rpm, 25 °C; discard supernatant and resuspend in 100 µl nuclear extract buffer (TD904, Vazyme). Incubate on ice 10 min, then centrifuge 6 min at 2500 rpm, 25 °C. Discard supernatant and resuspend nuclei in 100 µl wash buffer (TD904).

steps.title: Bind nuclei to ConA magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Activate Concanavalin A‑coated magnetic beads (TD904, Vazyme) and mix with 250 000 nuclei, 75 µl wash buffer (TD904) in a 200 µl tube. Incubate at room temperature for 10 min with 2–3 gentle inversions.

steps.title: Add primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a magnetic rack, discard supernatant, add 50 µl antibody buffer (TD904) to resuspend the bead–nucleus complex. Add 1 µl of each primary antibody (H3K9me3 Cat39161, H3K27me3 Cat39155, or H3K4me3 Cat39060; Active Motif) as required. Invert to mix, centrifuge briefly, then incubate statically at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Add secondary antibody and wash
steps.instruction: Prepare secondary mix: 0.5 µl secondary rabbit antibody (Ab207; Vazyme) in 49.5 µl Dig wash buffer (792 µl Wash Buffer + 8 µl 5 % Digitonin). Add to beads, rotate at 9–11 rpm/min at room temperature for 1 h. Wash the beads three times with 200 µl Dig wash buffer.

steps.title: Incubate transposase with Dig‑300
steps.instruction: Add 2 µl Hyperactive pA/G‑Transposon (TD904) to 98 µl Dig‑300 buffer (100 µl 10× Dig‑300 Buffer, 2 µl 5 % Digitonin, 20 µl 50× protease inhibitor, 878 µl ddH₂O). Rotate at 9–11 rpm/min at room temperature for 1 h. Place on magnetic rack, discard supernatant and wash three times with 200 µl Dig‑300 buffer.

steps.title: Tagment DNA (fragmentation)
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl TruePrep Tagment Buffer L (TD904) to 40 µl Dig‑300 buffer in each reaction. Incubate at 37 °C for 1 h.

steps.title: Extract DNA and add spike‑in
steps.instruction: Add 2 µl 10 % SDS and 0.5 µl DNA spike‑in (TD904) to each reaction, incubate 55 °C for 10 min. Transfer supernatant to a new tube, add 50 µl activated DNA extract beads (TD904), mix and incubate 20 min at room temperature. Wash beads twice with 200 µl 1× B&W buffer (TD904), dry briefly and resuspend in 30 µl RNase‑free ddH₂O.

steps.title: PCR amplify libraries
steps.instruction: Set up a 50 µl PCR: 15 µl bead‑bound DNA, 25 µl 2× CUT&Tag Amplification Mix (TD904), 5 µl N5XX primer (TD202), 5 µl N7XX primer (TD202). Thermocycle: 72 °C 3 min, 95 °C 3 min; then 9–20 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, 60 °C 5 s, 72 °C 1 min; hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Purify PCR products
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl VAHTS DNA clean beads (N411; Vazyme) to the PCR, incubate 5 min, wash twice with 200 µl 80 % ethanol, dry, resuspend in 22 µl RNase‑free ddH₂O and incubate 5 min before QC and sequencing.

steps.title: Optional formaldehyde crosslinking for protein targets
steps.instruction: Fix ~1 g fungal spores with 9 ml 0.1 % formaldehyde for 8 min at room temperature, quench with 1 ml 2 M glycine for 5 min, then wash three times with 20 ml 0.7 M NaCl. After the tagmentation step, reverse crosslinks by incubating overnight at 65 °C with 3 µl 5 M NaCl, then treat with RNase A at 37 °C for 30 min, Proteinase K at 53 °C for 1 h, and finally add protease inhibitors at room temperature for 5 min before proceeding to library PCR.
